issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'פַּחַת עֲבַֽר נַהֲרָה' means 'governor of Beyond-the-River' (a title/office), but the Chinese renders it as '過河處河的百夫長' ('centurion of the river-crossing place'), which misidentifies the office as a military rank and mistranslates the geographic name.
The Hebrew has 'תַּתְּנַי' (Tattenai) as the sender, but the Chinese renders it as '他特乃' (a transposition of characters, effectively a different name).
The Hebrew has 'שְׁתַר בּוֹזְנַי' (Shethar-bozenai), but the Chinese renders it as '示他博斯乃' (a transposition of '示他' and '博斯乃', effectively swapping the order of the two names).

The Hebrew 'וּכְנָוָתֵהּ' means 'and their associates/colleagues', but the Chinese renders it as '及其同伴' which is acceptable; however, the Hebrew 'אֲפַרְסְכָיֵא' (the Apharsachites) is rendered as '亞法薩迦' which is a transliteration but the Hebrew also includes 'דִּי בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָה' ('who were in Beyond-the-River') which is omitted in the Chinese.
